phases.title: Worlds that grow, and a Bazaar to build

tasks.title: Prosperity core: world tiers, needs by rule, need fill from sales
tasks.brief: Goal: every established world has a Prosperity tier and a need list; sales at the world fill its needs; progress and tier-ups happen at cycle end. Design: design/proposals/2026-11-06-empire-growth-v2.md section 3.1. Read: game/route_engine.gd (_run_local, _note_sale, sold_price), game/main.gd (_end_cycle, collect_state, apply_state), game/pathfinder.gd (post_built, platform_built), game/goods.gd (tier, branch_ok), data/goods.json, data/planet_types.json. Build game/prosperity.gd (owned by main) and data/prosperity.json: tier per planet (0 discovered, 1 once the post stands; dead worlds are Barren = -1 with no ladder yet, leave a hook for reclaim); need list by RULE: energy plus the run's branch goods whose goods.json tier <= world tier, minus goods the world already sells to the player (it has a <good>_buy price), capped by a per-tier count, ordered by planet-type weights from data/prosperity.json; optional per-planet override list. Demand per need per tier (keys prosperity_demand_t<N>). Count units sold at each planet per good per cycle where route_engine notes sales, and expose add_fill(planet, good, units) for the Flagship and hubs. At cycle end: every need met -> progress +1 step; any short -> progress minus prosperity_decay_steps, floor 0; full (prosperity_steps_t<N>) -> tier up and emit tier_up(planet, tier). A world never loses a tier. A need whose good is not visible counts as unmet and is reported as locked. UI API: tier(i), max_tier(), needs(i) -> [{good or '?', demand, sold, met, locked}], progress(i) 0..1, restless(i). Save and load (old saves: established worlds start at tier 1). No pricing (separate task), no rewards (separate task). Numbers: only data/balance.json keys with placeholder values, marked placeholder in the balance source note; economy-designer sets them later (owner starts it by hand); never put tuning numbers in code. Text: ids only (story source, python3 tools/build_story.py, English only; use StoryText.get_or fallbacks until the story task lands). tasks.title: Need pricing: a need opens a buyer, hunger premium, surplus price
tasks.brief: Goal: prices follow need, so the best lane moves as worlds grow and dumping stops paying. Design: design/proposals/2026-11-06-empire-growth-v2.md section 3.1 (Need pricing). Read: game/trade.gd (price), game/route_engine.gd (sold_price, local_price, route_margin, best_partner, forecast, project_storage), game/cash_forecast.gd, game/prosperity.gd, data/markets.json (base_value). Build a planet factor beside the event factor: (1) a need opens a sell price at a world that has none for that good (need price per tier = base_value x key need_price_t<N>); (2) hunger: each cycle a need is short its sell price rises by need_hunger_step_pct up to need_hunger_cap_pct, and settles back once met; (3) surplus: units sold above the need's demand in one cycle earn need_surplus_pct of the price; a key need_surplus_all (0/1, placeholder 0) extends surplus to every sale for the owner to try. Forecasts, margins and best-partner hints must use the same prices. Expose price_reason(planet, good) -> 'hungry' | 'surplus' | '' for the UI. Save hunger state.
